To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N-terminal domain, but not the C-terminal domain of Ca2+/CaM undergoes a screw axis rotation upon binding to a peptide.
CaM has a conformational plastic ability to adapt its structure to different target proteins.
the crystal structure of CaM complex with the peptide derived from the CaMKK kinase domain of C. elegans reveals the structural basis of target-induced conformational plastic of CaM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis for the conformational plasticities in CaM, which are required for the CaM-dependent regulation of diverse target proteins.
the conformational plasticities of CaM and the mechanism of its binding to various proteins.
the structural basis of the CaM-peptide interactions, which are essential for the regulation of Ca(2+)/CaM-dependent protein kinases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CaM is highly flexible in its interactions with target peptides.
the N-terminal domain is the most plastic domain of CaM, which is responsible for its multi-functional nature.
CaM has a certain degree of conformational adaptability, which is not only restricted to the C-terminal domain but extends also to the N-terminal domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CaM is capable of binding to various target proteins with a range of screw axis rotation angles.
, in the presence of Ca(2+), the N-terminal domain is more flexible than the C-terminal domain and is able to adapt to the binding of different peptides.
the CaM-binding peptide from CaMKK induces a 40 degrees screw axis rotation angle of the N-terminal domain relative to the C-terminal domain of Ca(2+)CaM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conformational plastic nature of CaM is not only limited to the C-terminal lobe of CaM, as previously thought, but also involves the N-terminal lobe of the molecule.
the CaMKK-binding peptide is the first example where CaM adopts a conformation that is significantly different from that seen in other Ca(2+)/peptide complexes.
the N-terminal domain is a major contributor in the conformational adaptation and plasticity of CaM.
